To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
individuals’ collective privacy on SNSs can be conceptualized as a multidimensional construct that includes concerns over information access, control, and diffusion.

(1) the collective privacy concerns of SNS users are composed of three dimensions, namely, collective access, collective control and collective diffusion, (2) the three dimensions of collective concerns are positively correlated, and (3) the three dimensions are positively correlated with individuals’ own privacy concerns.

this study provides a new theoretical framework of collective privacy concerns and develops and empirically validates a preliminary measure of SNS users collective privacy concerns.

the collective privacy concerns are an important construct to understand how individuals are concerned about their own privacy as well as the privacy of their social ties.
individuals’ collective privacy concern is not only a result of their own privacy concerns but also a result of their concern for their social ties’ privacy.
